questions.question: How do modern software cars track how drivers use built-in apps?
options: By asking drivers to fill out weekly paper forms.
By measuring actual usage data when drivers give permission.
By guessing usage patterns from old car models.
By scanning driver fingerprints to log app access times.
questions.explanation: SDVs collect real usage data when drivers agree, which helps makers build better features faster.

questions.question: Why did Nokia lose market share because of its operating systems?
options: It delayed software updates for years after phone release.
It created many different systems that did not work together.
It removed all app stores from its mobile devices.
It focused only on hardware and ignored internet services.
questions.explanation: Too many incompatible systems confused developers and users, which broke the app market.

questions.question: What causes extreme software fragmentation in today's cars?
options: Dealerships change software rules for each new customer.
Car makers use custom parts and code from many different suppliers.
Government laws force every car to use different security checks.
Drivers install personal apps that block factory software updates.
questions.explanation: Many suppliers provide different hardware and code, so apps cannot easily run on multiple car models.

questions.question: What job do standardized vehicle APIs perform for developers?
options: They translate legacy database records into modern cloud formats.
They give a fixed way to talk to car systems across different models.
They compile raw engine data into visual dashboard graphics.
They automatically route customer complaints to regional service centers.
questions.explanation: Fixed APIs let programmers write code once and use it in many cars without rewriting it.

questions.question: How does the hardware abstraction layer help car software run properly?
options: It stores all driver preferences in a single cloud database.
It connects the code to different physical parts and keeps the system steady.
It manages real-time braking signals during emergency stops.
It encrypts navigation routes to prevent GPS tracking.
questions.explanation: HAL acts as a bridge so software works on many different hardware designs without changes.

questions.question: Why do engineers need a strong software stack for cars?
options: It compiles driver preference profiles into local storage files.
It lets programs interact smoothly with vehicle parts and supports new features.
It routes diagnostic error codes to mobile technician apps.
It synchronizes media playback across multiple vehicle speakers.
questions.explanation: A solid software stack connects code to hardware, making it easier to add and run new innovations.

questions.question: How can car makers keep their unique features while using shared software rules?
options: They can standardize most common tools and keep special tools for themselves.
They can sell all software code to other companies for a high fee.
They can remove all internet access to protect customer privacy.
They can force drivers to visit a shop for every single update.
questions.explanation: Making 70-80% of APIs standard saves time, while keeping 20-30% private allows each brand to stand out.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using harmonized APIs across different car brands?
options: It requires all developers to use the same programming language.
It allows data to move smoothly between cars, services, and drivers.
It unifies the billing process for third-party app subscriptions.
It aligns warranty terms for software updates across brands.
questions.explanation: Shared rules let information flow easily between drivers, services, and different car companies.

questions.question: How does opening up software access help solve complex driving challenges?
options: It centralizes all regional traffic data in a single government server.
It lets programmers worldwide share ideas and build better automated systems.
It bans all foreign software from entering the domestic car market.
It limits software updates to only one major release per decade.
questions.explanation: Open access creates a global marketplace where many developers can work on hard driving problems together.

questions.question: What does a cloud-native approach allow software companies to do?
options: It bundles all application code into a single monolithic executable.
It uses internet computing rules to grow fast and stay stable under heavy load.
It requires developers to write code on paper before testing it.
It locks software versions so they never change after release.
questions.explanation: Cloud-native uses internet rules to help software adapt quickly, handle huge traffic, and stay reliable.

questions.question: Why are microservices useful for large software teams?
options: They let different groups change small parts of the system at different speeds.
They force all programmers to work on the same code file at the same time.
They remove all security checks to speed up the final product launch.
They store every line of code in a single public library.
questions.explanation: Microservices separate code into small pieces, so teams can update their parts without breaking everything else.

questions.question: What role do containers play in cloud-native software?
options: They compile raw sensor data into visual dashboard graphics.
They wrap programs in lightweight packages that run safely on many network computers.
They block all internet traffic to prevent outside hackers from entering.
They automatically print paper copies of every code update for archives.
questions.explanation: Containers package software so it runs consistently across different computers, offering speed and security.

questions.question: How do DevOps practices improve modern software development?
options: They let cross-team groups release small, reliable code changes frequently.
They require one person to test every line of code before shipping.
They delay all software releases until every possible bug disappears.
They separate developers from managers so each group works in silence.
questions.explanation: DevOps teams work together to push safe updates often, keeping pace with fast market needs.

questions.question: What did the open source community provide to build the modern internet?
options: It designed proprietary encryption standards for commercial banking.
It created secure and scalable tools like operating systems and container networks.
It banned all free software to protect company profits from loss.
It developed standardized network protocols for global data routing.
questions.explanation: Open source groups built reliable foundations like Linux and Docker that support most modern applications.

questions.question: How do companies make money from open source software today?
options: They sell extra support, training, and special services around the free code.
They charge users a high monthly fee to download the base program.
They lock the code behind a paywall so only rich buyers can see it.
They offer premium consulting packages for enterprise system integration.
questions.explanation: Companies keep the core code free but earn revenue by offering professional help and custom features.

questions.question: What is the main goal of the Eclipse SDV working group?
options: It develops standardized safety protocols for autonomous braking systems.
It builds a shared open platform to speed up car software innovation.
It creates open-source toolchains for continuous integration pipelines.
It manages global licensing agreements for proprietary navigation maps.
questions.explanation: Eclipse SDV creates a public software foundation that helps many developers improve vehicle systems faster.

questions.question: What job does an app store perform for vehicle software?
options: It verifies digital signatures to ensure software authenticity.
It acts as a central hub where users can easily download third-party programs.
It manages subscription renewals for premium navigation services.
It aggregates user feedback to prioritize future feature updates.
questions.explanation: App stores gather many programs in one place, making it simple for users to install useful tools.

questions.question: Why do simple programming languages matter for car app creators?
options: They let newcomers build programs quickly without studying complex old systems.
They force developers to learn five different coding styles at once.
They remove all safety warnings so programmers can test dangerous features.
They require every app to run on a single specific car model.
questions.explanation: Easy languages lower the learning barrier, so more people can create useful car tools fast.

questions.question: Why do car makers face a harder challenge than smartphone makers with software?
options: Cars must handle strict safety rules and instant response needs.
Cars sell for much lower prices than smartphones do today.
Cars do not use any wireless signals or internet connections.
Cars require developers to install software on physical paper cards.
questions.explanation: Vehicles need fast processing for safety, so software must work instantly and never fail during driving.

questions.question: What happens when companies collaborate on non-differentiating software parts?
options: They save time and money to focus on features that customers actually want.
They lose all control over their product quality and safety standards.
They force every driver to use the exact same navigation routes.
They prevent any company from ever releasing a new software update.
questions.explanation: Sharing basic tools frees up resources, so companies can spend more effort on unique customer features.
